system.description:
This is sometimes called a “jet pack,” and is a one-person wearable vehicle that allows the user to fly by jet propulsion. Thrusters on the back and controlled by the hands provide flight and steering. It normally flies at GEV heights of a few yards over the ground but can theoretically reach a ceiling of 2000 feet. The disadvantages of a flight pack are its limited flight time (20 minutes before refueling) and the fact that it requires the operator’s constant attention. You must always use the Run/Chase major action, even when hovering in mid-air, or you will fall. Attacks on the flight pack also damage its wearer and force them to make a TN 13 Dexterity (Acrobatics) test to retain control or fall. The first test does not require an action, but subsequent tests after a failure each require a minor action.
